title: DMA 64-byte descriptor memory layout
note: Byte offsets increase left to right within 16-byte rows. Little-endian words; arrays are expanded into their actual elements. Gold is software configuration, blue-gray is result writeback, and gray is reserved. Control/ownership words may contain both software and hardware bits; use the field contract before modifying them.

title: APUMC 64-byte fixed header
note: Little-endian 32-bit words. The CRC covers the bytes after this fixed header. Three entry descriptors begin at byte 64; instructions begin at byte 192, after descriptor/alignment space. This format does not establish delivery of a production codec image.

title: APUMC 32-byte codec entry descriptor
note: Each entry has eight little-endian words. Word 0: format in bits 3:0 and entry PC above bit 3. Word 1: first/last PC in low/high 16 bits. Word 7: table offset/size in low/high 16 bits. Actual PC, scratch and table bounds are checked by the existing packager/loader.

title: HP boot bundle fixed-header byte layout
note: Fields and offsets are taken from the same packager/loader comparison as the tables below. Words are little-endian; flash offsets are absolute within the flash image, while bundle total size is relative to the bundle start.

title: HP boot bundle payload-descriptor byte layout
note: Fields and offsets are taken from the same packager/loader comparison as the tables below. Words are little-endian; flash offsets are absolute within the flash image, while bundle total size is relative to the bundle start.

title: UART serial framing: data slots and optional framing bits
note: Two examples show wire slots, not register bits: 8N1 and 8E2. Data is sent least-significant bit first; the parity slot is omitted when disabled. The controller supports 5-8 data bits, configured parity and one/two stop bits. Baud timing and error reporting remain in the existing timing diagrams.

title: I2C 12-bit command FIFO entry
note: This is the internal command entry, distinct from the 32-bit APB access. READ changes the byte operation; RESTART/STOP request bus transitions and NACK_LAST selects the final receive acknowledgement.

title: I2C address and data-byte transfer groups
note: Groups are shown in transmission order, with data bits MSB first. START/repeated START/STOP are bus transitions outside these bit groups. ACK/NACK occupies the ninth clock. Ten-bit read sequencing additionally uses the repeated address prefix described by the controller state machine.

rows.label: Address low byte / ordinary data byte

title: WS2812 GRB pixel word and transmission order
note: The helper builds a 24-bit GRB value. Green is sent first, starting at bit 23; the core emits bit timing and the reset interval separately. The upper eight bits of the APB write are not an additional color channel.

title: PS/2 serial frame slots
note: Serial slots run left to right: start, eight data bits LSB first, odd parity, stop. Host inhibit, filtering, timeout and frame-error policy remain part of the implementation contract; this diagram is not a timing measurement.

title: Native SD short and long response field groups
note: The first received bit is the leftmost field. Short responses contain 48 bits; long R2 responses contain 136 bits. Response type controls CRC/index checking, and R1b adds a separate DAT0 busy interval. CID/CSD payload semantics are not expanded into unrelated device-specific register claims.

title: SD 48-bit command content
note: Native SDIO and SPI-SD share this command content; clocking, CS, response and busy framing follow their separate protocol chapters.

shared_notes.spisd: SPI-SD uses the same 48-bit command content; its CS, stuff-byte, response and busy framing remain SPI-mode behavior.

title: SDIO data word byte lanes
note: Memory/PIO lane 0 (bits 7:0) is the first byte placed on the SD wire. Each byte is transferred MSB first; a four-bit bus carries its high nibble before its low nibble. KEEP/STRB describes valid memory lanes and is not a transmitted CRC field.

title: SPI-SD response groups
note: MSB-first response groups, after command/stuff-byte handling. R1b adds a separate MISO busy interval. R3/R7 append a 32-bit payload to R1; R2 appends a second status byte. These are SPI-mode responses, not native SDIO response words.

title: SPI-SD single-block token, payload and CRC example
note: A 512-byte data-block example, compressed horizontally and not to scale. Single-block data uses token 0xFE; multi-block write uses 0xFC and a separate stop token. Bytes are sent MSB first. The programmed block size and CRC policy remain authoritative.

title: USB2 token bytes presented after the PID
note: The SIE supplies the token low byte, then token high bits plus CRC5. The separate ULPI TX command selects a 4-bit PID; the external PHY supplies wire PID/framing. SETUP/IN/OUT tokens use address/endpoint bits; SOF uses a frame number in the same 11-bit token container.

title: USB2 data-packet payload and CRC example
note: Eight payload bytes are illustrative; packet length follows the active transfer. The SIE sends finished CRC16 low byte before high byte. PID/SYNC/EOP belong to the PHY-facing framing path and are not bytes in this payload buffer. Handshake packets have no payload; zero-length data still has CRC.

title: XPI 16-bit LUT instruction format
note: This is a serial-controller LUT instruction, not a CPU instruction or a register bit-layout replacement. Two instructions occupy one APB word, lower instruction first. Opcode selects command/address/mode/dummy/TX/RX/stop behavior; PADS selects the lane count.

title: Single-clock HyperBus command/address field layout
note: 48-bit CA is sent most-significant byte first. R/W is the inverse of write; Space selects register access and Linear is 1. The controller forms word address from byte address shifted right by one. This single-clock profile is not a claim of external HyperBus compliance.

title: OPI command-byte and address-byte ordering
note: One- or two-byte command and three- or four-byte address are selected by the configured profile. The two strips are independent examples. Dummy/wait phases and DQS policy are timing controls, not extra address bytes.

title: QPI command and chip-local address fields
note: Address-bearing commands send an eight-bit opcode and a 24-bit address field whose top bit is zero. The remaining 23 bits are chip-local address bits. Single/quad lane timing, dummy phases, chip selection and data phases are separate from this field layout.

title: AES/SHA payload byte lanes
note: Little-endian APB/AXI lanes: lane 0 is earliest. Valid KEEP/PSTRB is a contiguous low-byte mask: 0001, 0011, 0111 or 1111. AES key/IV word 0 contains the first four API bytes; FIPS byte ordering is applied inside the engine.

title: SHA digest word ordering
note: Digest word 0 is the most significant digest word. SHA-256 uses eight words; SHA-224 uses seven meaningful words and returns zero in word 7. This word significance differs from RSA limb significance.

bindings.text: SHA digest word 0 is the most significant digest word.

title: RSA 2048-bit operand limb ordering
note: 64 little-endian 32-bit limbs; word 0 is least significant and word 63 is most significant. The middle 60 words are collapsed in this schematic. Public/private exponent rules and operand validity remain those of the RSA contract.
